PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR LICENSING — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR LICENSING — INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Private Investigator Act, Business and Professions Code Sections 7512 through 7573.5, which governs who must hold a private investigator license issued by the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services before engaging in the business of investigating specified categories of information, including investigations into an employer's own employees' honesty, integrity, or job performance. Acme, Inc. has described its use of investigative services, if any, as follows: We are considering engaging a firm to conduct pre-employment background investigations on finalist candidates. This document states the content of the statute; it does not determine whether any particular individual, engagement, or investigative activity meets the statutory definition of "private investigator" or falls within a statutory exemption, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice or for consulting a licensed attorney.

STATUTORY DEFINITION OF "PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR"
Business & Professions Code § 7521 defines a "private investigator" as a person who, for consideration, engages in business or accepts employment to make any investigation for the purpose of obtaining information about specified categories, including the identity, habits, conduct, honesty, integrity, credibility, trustworthiness, or character of any person, or to secure evidence to be used before a court, board, officer, or investigating committee. The statute states that a private investigator, for purposes of the section, includes a person acting to investigate, obtain, and report to an employer, or an agent designated by the employer, information concerning the employer's employees involving questions of integrity, honesty, breach of rules, or other standards of performance of job duties.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The identity, habits, conduct, business, occupation, honesty, integrity, credibility, knowledge, trustworthiness, efficiency, loyalty, activity, movement, whereabouts, affiliations, associations, transactions, acts, reputation, or character of any person."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7521 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7521 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7521)
  "For the purposes of this section, a private investigator is any person, as defined in Section 7512.3, acting for the purpose of investigating, obtaining, and reporting to any employer, or an agent designated by the employer, information concerning the employer’s employees involving questions of integrity, honesty, breach of rules, or other standards of performance of job duties."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7521 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7521 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7521)
  Known gap: This information sheet does not classify any specific investigative engagement a reader is considering as falling within or outside this definition; that determination depends on the precise scope of the work performed and the consideration paid for it, which are fact questions this document does not resolve.

LICENSE REQUIRED TO ENGAGE IN THE BUSINESS OF PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR
Business & Professions Code § 7520 prohibits a person from engaging in a business regulated by the Private Investigator Act, or from acting or representing themselves as a licensee, unless licensed under the chapter. Section 7523(a) restates this requirement specifically as applied to the business of private investigator: unless exempted under Section 7522, a person may not engage in the business of private investigator, as defined in Section 7521, unless that person has applied for and received a license to engage in that business.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "No person shall engage in a business regulated by this chapter; act or assume to act as, or represent himself or herself to be, a licensee unless he or she is licensed under this chapter; and no person shall falsely represent that he or she is employed by a licensee."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7520 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7520 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7520)
  "Unless specifically exempted by Section 7522, no person shall engage in the business of private investigator, as defined in Section 7521, unless that person has applied for and received a license to engage in that business pursuant to this chapter."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7523(a) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7523(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7523)
  Known gap: This information sheet does not confirm whether any particular vendor a reader is considering engaging currently holds an active license; license status can be verified only through the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services' own licensee records, which this document does not reproduce.

LIABILITY FOR KNOWINGLY ENGAGING AN UNLICENSED INVESTIGATOR
Business & Professions Code § 7523(b) makes it a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of five thousand dollars or imprisonment in the county jail for up to one year, or both, for any person who violates the chapter's licensure provisions or who knowingly engages a nonexempt unlicensed person to perform private investigator services. Section 7523(c) authorizes the Attorney General, a district attorney, or a city attorney to bring a proceeding to impose that fine, with the collected penalty divided between the county and city treasuries depending on which office brings the action, or deposited into the Private Security Services Fund when brought by the Attorney General.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Any person who violates any provision of this chapter or who conspires with another person to violate any provision of this chapter, relating to private investigator licensure, or who knowingly engages a nonexempt unlicensed person is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of five thousand dollars ($5,000) or by imprisonment in the county jail not to exceed one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7523(b) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7523(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7523)
  Known gap: This clause addresses only the misdemeanor exposure Section 7523(b) creates for a party that knowingly engages an unlicensed, nonexempt private investigator; it does not address separate civil remedies, contract-based liability, or professional discipline that may also apply, and it does not determine whether any particular level of knowledge about a vendor's licensure status would satisfy the statute's 'knowingly' requirement in a specific case.

EXEMPTION FOR A PERSON EMPLOYED EXCLUSIVELY BY ONE EMPLOYER FOR INTERNAL, UNARMED INVESTIGATION
Business & Professions Code § 7522(a) states that the Private Investigator Act does not apply to a person employed exclusively and regularly by an employer who does not provide contract security services for other entities or persons, in connection with the affairs of that employer only, where an employer-employee relationship exists, if that person at no time carries or uses any deadly weapon in the performance of that person's duties. The statute defines "deadly weapon" for this purpose to include firearms, a dirk, dagger, any knife with a blade longer than five inches, and several other specified instruments.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A person employed exclusively and regularly by any employer who does not provide contract security services for other entities or persons, in connection with the affairs of that employer only and where there exists an employer-employee relationship if that person at no time carries or uses any deadly weapon in the performance of that person’s duties. For purposes of this subdivision, “deadly weapon” is defined to include any instrument or weapon of the kind commonly known as a blackjack, slungshot, billy, sandclub, sandbag, metal knuckles, any dirk, dagger, pistol, revolver, or any other firearm, any knife having a blade longer than five inches, any razor with an unguarded blade and any metal pipe or bar used or intended to be used as a club."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7522(a) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7522(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7522)
  Known gap: This information sheet does not determine whether any specific role a reader is considering — whether an internal investigator, human resources employee, or loss-prevention staff member — satisfies every element of this exemption, including the 'exclusively and regularly,' the 'employer-employee relationship,' and the 'no contract security services for others' requirements, each of which depends on the specific facts of the position.

OTHER NAMED EXEMPTIONS FROM THE LICENSING REQUIREMENT
Business & Professions Code § 7522 lists additional categories of persons to whom the Private Investigator Act does not apply. Among them: an attorney at law performing the attorney's duties as an attorney at law; a person engaged exclusively in the business of obtaining and furnishing information as to the financial rating of persons; and an individual registered as a process server under Section 22350, with respect to the act of serving process.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An attorney at law in performing the attorney’s duties as an attorney at law."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7522(e) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7522(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7522)
  "A person engaged exclusively in the business of obtaining and furnishing information as to the financial rating of persons."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7522(c) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7522(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7522)
  "The act of serving process by an individual who is registered as a process server pursuant to Section 22350."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7522(m) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7522(m) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7522)
  Known gap: This clause lists only a subset of the exemptions stated in Section 7522; the full statute contains additional categories — including exemptions for certain government employees, licensed insurance adjusters, banks, savings associations, secured creditors engaged in repossession, and specified labor-management committees — not restated here, and it does not determine whether any exemption applies to any particular vendor or arrangement.

LICENSURE QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE APPLICANT OR QUALIFIED MANAGER
Business & Professions Code § 7526 requires that, before a license application is granted, the applicant or the applicant's qualified manager be at least 18 years of age, not have committed acts or crimes constituting grounds for denial of a license under Section 480, comply with the requirements specified in the chapter for the particular license sought, and comply with other qualifications the director may fix by rule.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Before an application for a license is granted, the applicant for a license or his or her qualified manager shall meet all of the following:(a) Be at least 18 years of age.(b) Not have committed acts or crimes constituting grounds for denial of a license under Section 480.(c) Comply with the requirements specified in this chapter for the particular license for which an application is made.(d) Comply with other qualifications as the director may fix by rule."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7526 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7526 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7526)
  Known gap: This information sheet does not reproduce the separate grounds-for-denial standards of Business & Professions Code Section 480 referenced in subdivision (b), nor any rules the director has adopted under subdivision (d); both would need to be consulted directly, and are outside the scope of this document, to assess a specific applicant's eligibility.

FINGERPRINT-BASED FBI BACKGROUND CHECK AS PART OF THE LICENSE APPLICATION
Business & Professions Code § 7525.1(e)(1) requires that a license application include, for the applicant, a qualified manager, or specified partners, officers, or members, a personal identification form with a photograph and two legible sets of fingerprints, one of which is forwarded to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for purposes of a background check on a form approved by the Department of Justice, together with residence addresses and employment history for the previous five years, signed under penalty of perjury.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If the applicant is an individual, a qualified manager, a partner of a partnership, an officer of a corporation designated in subdivision (h), or a member, officer, or manager of a limited liability company designated in subdivision (i), one personal identification form provided by the bureau upon which shall appear a photograph taken within one year immediately preceding the date of the filing of the application together with two legible sets of fingerprints, one set of which shall be forwarded to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for purposes of a background check, on a form approved by the Department of Justice, and a personal description of each person, respectively. The identification form shall include residence addresses and employment history for the previous five years and be signed under penalty of perjury."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7525.1(e)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7525.1(e)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&division=3.&chapter=11.3.&article=3.)
  Known gap: This describes the background-check step built into the license applicant's own application to the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services; it does not describe any separate background check that a business engaging a private investigator's services might itself conduct on that investigator or the investigator's staff, a subject this section does not address.

LICENSEE'S RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CONDUCT OF EMPLOYEES AND AGENTS
Business & Professions Code § 7531 states that a licensee is legally responsible at all times for the good conduct in the business of each of the licensee's employees or agents, including the licensee's qualified manager.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A licensee shall at all times be legally responsible for the good conduct in the business of each of his or her employees or agents, including his or her qualified manager."
  — Business and Professions Code § 7531 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7531 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=7531)
  Known gap: This states the licensee's own statutory responsibility for its employees' and agents' conduct under the Private Investigator Act; it does not address a client business's separate contractual or vicarious liability for the acts of an investigator it engages, which is governed by ordinary contract and tort principles not restated in this chapter.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding California's Private Investigator Act, Business and Professions Code Sections 7512 through 7573.5, was prepared by Jordan T. Reyes for Acme, Inc. and reviewed in Oakland, California on September 6, 2026. It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked in each authority section below and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.

Reviewed by (on behalf of Acme, Inc.): ______________________
